brief: Goldman's weekly flow note argues investors remain structurally underweight the market even as SPX made a Tuesday all-time high, and the desk expects the next leg of chasing to show up through call options rather than net buying or put protection (dubbed 'FOBU'). Evidence: Tuesday's break of the SPX 7800 gamma wall drove the busiest bullish options stretch in months, 25-delta call vol stayed bid even as spot pulled back, and hedge fund net exposure, though up slightly to the 4th percentile over 3 years, remains near historic lows while gross exposure and VIX-over-SPX skew both point to chasing convexity rather than hedging it. The desk recommends 30-October expiry calls on SPX/SPY/QQQ/IWM, which capture the Fed, data and ~65% of earnings without paying for midterm risk. Separate trades: EWZ long into a Brazil catalyst, a biotech positioning opportunity, a long-ITA/short-XLI defense pair, and outperformance options betting non-AI names (RSP, SPXXAI) catch up to SPX even if markets fall. Financials are underperforming into earnings despite cheap implied moves, and the desk's favored AI theme is the power bottleneck via basket GSENEPOW.
